summary: 1. High-stayed (>51%) videos deliver a immediate, provocative claim in 10 words or fewer, whereas low-stayed (<36%) videos start with passive background narrative or long-winded setups. 2. Top-performing titles directly ask a relatable or high-curiosity question (e.g., 'Could A T. rex Outrun Your Car?'), while low-performing titles rely on niche technical explanations ('Why Highway Guardrails Have Heavy End Boxes'). 3. High stayed-rate hooks create immediate personal connection or visceral imagery using second-person addressing ('Your eyes are leaking right now') or vivid comparisons ('three small cars stacked on its teeth'). 4. Topics focusing on pop culture/dinosaurs and body trivia dramatically outperform engineering and niche astronomy in retention and initial reach. 5. Ideal duration for retention and engagement is under 25 seconds; longer standard videos (30-36s) suffer from drop-offs unless the hook resolves instantly.
winning_hooks: State a direct counter-intuitive reality in under 10 words (e.g., 'The real T. rex probably couldn't run. Not even a jog.')
Use direct second-person present tense accusations (e.g., 'Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.')
Use concrete absurd visual comparisons (e.g., 'pressed down like three small cars stacked on its teeth')
avoid: Narrative setup or setting scenes (e.g., 'Your car swerves off the highway right toward...')
Academic background preambles (e.g., 'Fossilized bones can last millions of years, but sometimes...')
Niche engineering/infrastructure topics lacking immediate personal relevance
next_experiment: A/B test the exact same video script with two hook styles: Test a direct personal claim ('Your body is doing X right now') vs. a scenario setup ('Imagine if X happened to you') to measure the exact impact on 3-second stayed_pct.
